subject: Private vs Dedicated: hosting decision and deal-linked GPU sizing for Sentinel Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads — quick sizing questions

Hi Anika — great speaking earlier. As promised, sketching a quick set of questions that will help us recommend Dedicated reserved capacity vs a Private (VPC/on-prem) package for the pilot and first-year rollout. Can you confirm the following so we can size accurately?

- Expected 95th percentile concurrent requests for inference during peak (per region) — or an RPS estimate and average prompt length.
- Average prompt + response token estimate (tokens).
- Max acceptable 95th percentile latency (ms) — e.g., 100ms, 250ms.
- Data residency / network isolation constraints (do you require customer-managed VPC and no shared underlying host?).
- Any procurement constraints (PO timeline, vendor legal review windows)?

If you prefer, we can run two side-by-side proposals (Dedicated reserved pool with SLA vs Private host bundle). Marcus will draft a capacity sketch once we have these numbers.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@sentinelhealth.com>

Cc: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@sentinelhealth.com>, procurement@sentinelhealth.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads — quick sizing questions

Hi Olga — thanks, quick answers below from our side:

- Peak concurrent requests: ~60 concurrent in US-east region during business hours, expected burst to 120 for scheduled batch loads.
- Typical prompt+response: ~350 tokens average (some longer clinical notes up to 1,200 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 250ms 95th for interactive clinician flows; background batch jobs can be higher.
- Isolation: We need full network isolation for PHI; customer-managed VPC preferred, but we are open to Dedicated reserved capacity if it provides tenancy isolation and clear SaaS-in-scope guarantees.
- Procurement: PO + legal review — ~6–8 weeks lead. Decision deadline: end of September for pilot kick-off.

Happy to sync if you need clarifications.
Anika
Anika Shah
Dir. AI Platform, Sentinel Health
anika.shah@sentinelhealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads — quick sizing questions

Olga / Marissa — based on Anika's numbers I ran a quick capacity sketch. Notes and assumptions below; I'll attach a delta workbook.

Assumptions:
- Model family: mix of 7B–13B instruction-tuned models (quantized), avg generation length 250 tokens, prompt 100 tokens → 350 tokens total.
- Token throughput per GPU (A100-80GB equiv, optimized runtime): ~110k tokens/minute sustained for mixed seq lengths with batching.
- Concurrency -> tokens/sec: 60 concurrent * (350 tokens / 2s avg response) ≈ 10,500 tokens/sec peak sustained; burst 120 -> 21k tokens/sec for short periods.

Sizing sketch (headroom for KV cache and spikes):
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, multi-tenant-isolated): 8x A100-80GB equiv nodes for steady-state, scaled to 14 nodes for bursts; autoscale policy with warm standby.
- Private (VPC-managed single-tenant hosts): 12x A100-80GB equiv nodes recommended to give consistent latency and to avoid noisy-neighbor variance; could be tiled across two AZs for resilience.

Trade-offs:
- Dedicated: lower committed cost (shared underlying infra) and easier autoscaling; requires contract language around isolation guarantees.
- Private: higher base cost but best latency predictability and simplifies compliance if Sentinel must control networking and KMS.

I'll attach sentinel-dedicated-sizing.xlsx with token models, expected QPS, and monthly cost bands for each option. If we assume a 12-month commitment, per-unit TCO favors Dedicated; if Sentinel requires custom KMS and full host-level isolation, Private is the path.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachments: sentinel-dedicated-sizing.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@sentinelhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads — quick sizing questions

Anika — looping in pricing notes and a rapid procurement checklist so you can share with your buying team. Key bullets: 

- Dedicated Reserved Pool (recommended pilot): 12-month commit with a 30% discount vs on-demand; includes SLA (99.9% per-route uptime), standard KMS integration, and audit logs. Add-on: tenant isolation addendum possible for additional cost.
- Private (VPC / On-prem): one-time onboarding + higher monthly resource fee (~1.6x of equivalent dedicated cost). Includes customer KMS/HSM options, extended audit retention, and on-prem installer if needed.
- Procurement timeline: We can provide PO-ready SOW and a pre-filled security appendix. Legal typically completes review in 3 weeks once the security appendix is agreed.

Next steps: I suggest a quick call with Bryan (technical ops at Sentinel) and procurement to align the legal ask and preferred infra. Olga — can you coordinate?

Thanks, Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. GTM Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:18:00 +0000
Subject: Next step: PO template and SOW for pilot (SENT-2026-082)

Hi Sentinel procurement team — per Anika's timeline, attaching a PO template and a draft SOW for the 3-month pilot (covers Dedicated and Private BAU options). Highlights:

- Pilot scope: 2x A100 equiv nodes reserved (pilot steady-state), auto-burst path to pool; pilot pricing and conversion credits laid out in SOW.
- Security appendix: VPC/KMS options enumerated; we can mark items where private hosting is required.
- Payment & billing cadence: monthly in arrears; PO processed to Redwood Inc.

Requested: please confirm a target PO date (we've penciled in 2026-09-15). Attachment: SENTINEL_MA_v1.pdf (MA + SOW stub).

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Cc: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@sentinelhealth.com>, procurement@sentinelhealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Next step: PO template and SOW for pilot (SENT-2026-082)

Thanks — we reviewed the SOW and the pilot approach internally. Good first pass. Two asks before we route to procurement: 

1) Can you add a line-item for a customer-managed KMS (we need HSM-backed keys for PHI encryption at rest)?
2) For Dedicated path, please add a short SLA clause clarifying tenant isolation and log export cadence (daily).

If you can update the SOW with those two items, procurement will aim for the 2026-09-15 PO date. We'll plan a kickoff the following week.

Thanks, Anika
